html:
The 1967 Hong Kong riots were months of strikes, riots and bombings in the British colony, led by local communists inspired by the Cultural Revolution in China.

They began in May with a labour dispute at a plastic flower factory. Leftists held mass protests waving the Little Red Book of Mao Zedong and called for the end of British rule. Over the summer they planted thousands of real and fake bombs. A popular radio host who mocked them, Lam Bun, was burned to death in his car. In all 51 people died.

Beijing did not back a takeover, and the movement lost public support. The government answered with reforms in the 1970s under governor Murray MacLehose: more public housing, free schooling, labour laws and an anti-corruption agency. Many date a distinct Hong Kong identity, apart from mainland China, to these years, later expressed in the films and music of the colony.
sum: The 1967 Hong Kong riots were months of strikes, riots and bombings in the British colony, led by local communists inspired by the Cultural Revolution in China.
